methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Vertical Semiconductor is a Seed-stage chip design company founded by Joshua Perozek, Cynthia Liao, and Tomas Palacios. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 11 private and public peers in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and private peers such as Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow peer set—the Chips & Semiconductors universe yielded only one adjacent-stage datapoint, below the threshold of three required for reliable triangulation. Consequently, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the subsequent financing round. Using the company's $11M total raised as a proxy for current value, this method implies a valuation of $28M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $23M to $32M, centered on $28M. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer benchmarks at equivalent stage and valuation tier, which limits calibration against market comparables. Additionally, the applicability of a 2.5x multiplier depends on execution velocity and market conditions specific to frontier semiconductor ventures, neither of which can be assessed from valuation data alone.
